[u][b]Update 1.6.4 is now live[/b][/u]

Hello beautiful people.I hope everyone is safe and doing well.

This update was focused on increasing the size of the terrain and making everything look nicer. 
The map has been completely rebuilt. The overall terrain is now 10 times larger than before. However, the playable area remains roughly the same. This change was needed to allow more room for places to explore as the game develops further. An example of this is how Hobart now has more houses than the entire game in the previous build. 

Also a lot of the models have been remade and the lighting has been adjusted to improve the look of the game.

There are two important side notes to mention. 
The first is that your previous saves will not work in the current build. You will need to delete them to be able to play.
The second is that the new build is aimed at higher end hardware then previously. You will need to adjust your quality settings in the main menu.

I hope you all enjoy the new build as much as I enjoyed making it for you. Stay beautiful and stay safe. Here are the patch notes.

--Patch 1.5.8--
Hello beautiful people
Alpha build 1.5.8 is now live. There are a few areas that were focused on for this one. Multi-language support is now implemented. Performance was another focus point. And adding small amounts of polish to a lot of different areas was another point of focus.
For this patch, I was able to get the game running a lot better and using a reduced amount of resources. As a result, I was able to lower the minimum requirements for the game. Also install size was reduced significantly.
I reached out to get some help from some other developers on the performance stuff in the shape of different ideas to try and would like to give a shout out to; Matt, Pat, High five, James and Matt W.
Some notes for this patch; old saves won’t work. It is recommended that people play either using Vsync or frame capping (It uses less GPU).
Let’s jump into the patch notes.

•	15 languages are now supported (English, Arabic -World, Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional, Czech, Danish -Denmark, French – France, German – Germany, Greek – Greece, Italian – Italy, Japanese – Japan, Portuguese – Portugal, Russian – Russia, Spanish – Spain, Swedish – Sweden) – This feature required re-writing every single script the game uses.

The game now uses a system that displays item Icons.

Game loading text has been mad much larger.

Collect water text made larger.

New on-screen text added for when you level up (telling you to spend skill points)

--CRAFTING / ITEM USE--
All items need to be in your hotbar to be used now.

To craft you now need to place materials into the crafting panels.

There is now a personal craft tab and a workbench crafting tab. Most items need you to first make a workbench.

--SOUNDS--
Fixed menu music bugs
Added button sounds to crafting panels.
Fixed Ambient sound bugs


--MOVEMENT--
Add in button modifier to allow reverse rotation on all the rotation buttons.

--ENEMIES--
Human enemies temporarily replaced with Mutants / Zombies.

The addition of Mutant / Zombie like enemies makes the game more challenging and added some stability)

--STABILITY--
The reason for the size of the patch is because I had to rebuild the entire game including a new exe to help add stability.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.content:
Hello again beautiful people.
This week I have mostly been working on the rebuild. This is because the rebuild has been moving along a lot quicker then I first expected. So, it made sense to not make things twice and just push the new version out faster.
I am very excited about the rebuild I have been adding in new stuff the live version doesn't have. 
I have been working on getting multiplayer, voice chat, controller support and cross platform support working right from the start.
I have also been working on a newer more polished looking GUI because this was one of the main things you beautiful people requested.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.content:
Hello Beautiful people

It’s that time of the week again where I give you guys an insight into the work I am doing.

So right now, on my end there are two versions of the game. There is the version that is available to you guys and the rebuild I am working on.

For the live version I have been working on doing my own custom weapons and fps animations. This is coming along nicely. You guys have requested a lot of changes to the game regarding the GUI. One request was hot bars for equipping weapons and items. So, I decided to start with the weapons because I am wanting to add extra features like; barehanded, zooming/aiming and scoped weapons. And I want to add weapons to the hotbars as a point of testing.

For the rebuild version I have begun the process of migrating the project to a new engine. I have weighed the pros and cons and there are some issues that will be easily resolved by a newer engine and there are extra features that will be more easily added by a newer engine.

I just want to say thank you to all the people that have bought the game and supported the development. It’s because of you guys that I can keep this project going. I love you all you are amazing.

My personal situation is still in a transition stage at the current moment. The internet where I am staying is not great. I am taking advantage of this and working offline and completing as much new content as possible to both live and the rebuild. This way once I get some decent internet I will be able to upload a more significant patch. 

The new patch is likely to be a couple of weeks to a month away. But I will still post regular updates along the way to keep you lovely people informed.

Once the rebuild is fully migrated and a little further along I will start adding graphical content to the weekly updates. Because I value everyone’s feedback. 

Once the rebuild goes live the strategy will continue. Where I ask you guys for feedback and add the things you want. 

My vision for this game is to engage as much as possible with you guys and build the game that you guys want. I feel like this strategy works because as a developer I can get a bit singularly focused and you guys give me ideas that I would never have thought of. 
A good example of this was the key binds. I had been so focused on getting controller support working that I hadn't even considered custom key binds. Then a left-handed customer said I need this. And now that its added I love it and think it makes the game so much better.
I want to continue this trend moving forward in all my projects. Plus, I hate the way larger companies don't do this and kind of ignore players until they start losing money.

Sorry I rambled a bit on this one. 
I hope you all have a lovely week. And I look forward to hearing from you guys in the forums because it’s your input that is going to make this game awesome.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.content:
Its Friday which means it is time for the weekly update. This week has been both a good and slow kind of week.

So, patch 4 released earlier in the week. This was good because it added in skills and inventory management. Patch 4 meant I had to remake the store page trailer. I made a few versions of this and eventually decided you guys probably don't want to hear me talking about the game. So, I just went with a gameplay video with some background music.

So, the reason the skills were done the way they are is because I felt like it would allow players to balance the game as they see fit. Right now, the game is single player, so I decided not to cap skills. This means that if players want to cheat. They don't have to download or buy cheats. You can just level up your skills until you get the desired effects.

You guys mentioned to me that you would prefer the game be more targeted for higher end pcs rather than low-end pcs. I took this on board and upgraded the work pc. This way I can improve graphical content and get things looking a lot nicer. I also added new Screenshots to the store page after upgrading so there were better quality pictures up.

The weather is still terrible here. So, I haven't had a chance to go and record those sounds and sound effects yet.

I have been thinking about the possibility of bringing multiplayer to this project once I have accomplished a few other things first. So, I was wondering what you guys think and what style of multiplayer you guys would prefer? I was thinking maybe a simple system that’s a little private (using P2P peer networking, and you must invite people to your game), instead of a lobby or server list style.

So, moving forward I am going to be focusing on; graphical content (textures, shadows etc.), animations and sounds. 

If you guys can think of anything you want added to the game, please hit the discussion forums in the survey section and let me know.
